behavior: Clings upright to trunks, bracing with its stiff tail. Drills orderly rows of sap wells and returns to lap sap and trapped insects; also gleans insects from bark, catches some in flight, and drums in a stuttering rhythm.
field_marks: Bold black-and-white facial stripes with a red forehead
Male has a red throat; female has a white throat
Long white patch along each folded black wing
Whitish underparts with a pale yellow belly wash and dark chest crescent
Stout, straight, dark bill and dark eye
Gray feet and a stiff, pointed black tail adapted for trunk-clinging
habitat: Hardwood and mixed coniferous forests, especially young woods, forest edges, and groves of small deciduous trees; outside the breeding season also uses open woodland, orchards, and other semi-open wooded habitats.
